Body:
Root cause confirmed to be opentui-side: the unguarded module-scope top-level `await resolveBundledFilePath(...)` added in `@opentui/core@0.4.5`, whose result flows into `normalizeLoadedFilePath` and calls `.startsWith` on an `undefined` worker path. Filed upstream: anomalyco/opentui#1275.

The opencode-side trigger is `packages/opencode/script/build.ts` listing `parser.worker.js` as a `Bun.build` entrypoint, which makes the `{ with: { type: "file" } }` import's `.default` `undefined`. So this is fixable here (drop that entrypoint) and/or upstream via #1275.

The reported V2 `undefined/chat/completions` / unsupported native OpenAI-compatible package path is resolved on the latest `v2` branch. `settings.baseURL` now reaches the native `openai-compatible-chat` route, bearer auth is preserved, and the built-in `@opencode-ai/ai/providers/openai-compatible` entrypoint is registered. Focused session model-resolution and OpenAI-compatible Chat route tests pass. Any provider-specific reasoning-option incompatibility should be tracked separately.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #35124: Same `400 Upstream request failed` error from the Zen/Console provider — may share the same underlying Zen API issue
- #37056: Also reports `400 Error from provider (Console): Upstream request failed` through the Zen gateway

If your issue is distinct (e.g., the Claude Code client sends requests in a format incompatible with the Zen API, rather than a model-specific or request-size issue), please clarify what differs so maintainers can track it separately.

Fixed by #37572. Managed background services no longer hold a lifetime flock: singleton ownership is now the exclusive bind on a deterministic per-channel TCP port. Concurrent starts probe the authenticated incumbent, stale registrations can be replaced, foreign port conflicts fail with an actionable error, and client startup retries are bounded instead of hanging forever.

Reproduced on 1.18.2 and dug into where the loop actually lives. One data point that may help scope the fix: the two open PRs (#34029, #34261) patch the core V2 runner (`packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts` and `packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts`), but the loop I captured runs through the session prompt path in `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, which is what the server prompt handler wires up. Unless I am misreading the wiring, those PRs will not cover it.

Evidence from my local DB: one long-running `opencode run` session recorded 35 consecutive assistant messages with `mode: "compaction"`, one every 30 to 90 seconds for over an hour. Every one of them finished `stop` with no error. So this is not only the summarizer-failure mode: each summary succeeded but did not shrink the request enough (we had `compaction.prune: false`, so giant old tool outputs stayed), the next turn overflowed, and `compaction.create` fired again with nothing bounding the cycle.

In `SessionPrompt` the mid-turn overflow path (`result === "compact"` -> `compaction.create`) has no attempt limit and no check that compaction reduced tokens, which is the same gap #34261 closes for the core runner.

What fixed it for us, in case it helps others:

1. `compaction.prune: true` so compaction can actually drop old tool outputs.
2. Pinning the built-in `compaction` agent to a large-context model so the summary prompt itself cannot overflow.
3. A small guard in the `SessionPrompt` loop: count consecutive overflow -> compaction cycles with no successful turn in between, and after 3, fail the message with `ContextOverflowError` instead of compacting again. Running this as a source patch since yesterday; the loop is gone and legitimate multi-compaction sessions still work because any productive turn resets the counter.

Happy to open a PR for the guard on the `SessionPrompt` path if maintainers want it, either standalone or rebased on top of #34261.

`#21550` is the closest prior case, but it was auto-closed for inactivity and its closing comment says to open a new issue if still relevant. `#20695` is focused on heap growth inside OpenCode; the allocator captured here was the spawned Node test child, so an OpenCode heap snapshot would not capture that child heap. `#20902` is an inherited-stdio/background-process hang, while this was an active foreground test process consuming host memory.
